findings.whyBlockerNotShouldFix: The key is named liveGateOwners. It does not describe a preference or a proposal; it asserts what the live register says, and it is false against the pinned file 08 whose digest this same artifact carries and which recomputes. Severity follows from what the artifact is for: an execution-remainder join exists to record who owns what remains after the design half closes. executionObligationOwnerToday is that record, and on four obligations it names a team that the register does not assign to this gate. A downstream reader taking this join at its word would route G07 execution to the wrong owner, which is the single substantive output of the document. This is not a wording imprecision that leaves the reader able to resolve the truth — the artifact supplies a confident, specific, wrong value, and the reader has no cue to distrust it.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: Nothing else in the artifact depends on this being right. The four corpus classes, the UNPOPULATED filesystem standing, the DR-103 non-theft obligations, the treeRootDigest reservation and every digest are all correct. The obligation set is coherent and correctly bucketed. This is a single false value with a mechanical propagation, not a structural defect.
findings.fix: Set liveGateOwners.DR-G07 to the live owner cell 'Security + platform', matching the subject's own pinned G07 v3, and propagate that value to executionObligationOwnerToday on the four obligations that currently carry the invented string. No other field needs to move.

observationsNotFindings: The finding is narrow and the fix is mechanical, but it is worth noting how it survived a cycle. The value is not a typo — 'Delivery + security / component architecture' is a plausible-sounding owner for an exact-bytes gate that sits next to DR-103, whose owner is 'Delivery + security'. It reads as if it were measured. That is precisely why a liveness-asserting field has to be compared rather than read: a wrong value that looks wrong gets caught, and a wrong value that looks right does not.

Everything the subject actually adds over its predecessor is correct. OBL-G07-INPUT-CORPUS is the new obligation, it is correctly measured leftoverDesign false, its reason correctly limits the close to the naming layer, and the g07-input-corpus.v1 verdict it rests on is genuinely ACCEPT 0/0. If the owner value were corrected, I see nothing else standing between this artifact and an ACCEPT.

The UNPOPULATED filesystem coverage domain is handled well and is the strongest part of the document. The subject not only declines to populate the set, it reproduces G07 v3's reason for the gap — that the live harness cell names 'supported filesystems' and no live governing source contains that set — and explicitly refuses the one available shortcut, routing the domain to G22 TCB filesystem selectors. Refusing a specific tempting wrong answer is stronger than a generic denial.

The chain is single-reviewer end to end: no Codex artifact exists for this leftover-join, for the G07 harness at any of its three versions, for the named-corpus catalog, or for the input corpus. Five of this subject's six pins are Claude verdicts, and one is mine. That concentration is what made the self-correction below necessary rather than merely tidy.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One blocker. liveGateOwners.DR-G07 reads 'Delivery + security / component architecture'. The live file 08 DR-G07 owner cell reads 'Security + platform'. The subject's own pinned G07 v3 — recomputed and matching — also carries 'Security + platform', so the artifact contradicts the specification it cites as live occupancy. The invented string occurs nowhere in docs/ except this artifact and its frozen predecessor, and it is propagated into executionObligationOwnerToday on four of the nine obligations. I graded it a blocker rather than a should-fix because recording who owns the remaining execution is the substantive output of an execution-remainder join, and the value is asserted confidently under a key whose name claims liveness, leaving a reader no cue to distrust it. The fix is mechanical: adopt 'Security + platform' in liveGateOwners and in the four obligations. Everything else is clean and the new material is correct — 12 of 12 basedOn pins and 13 of 13 recordedInputs recompute, all five cited Claude verdicts were opened and are genuinely ACCEPT 0/0, the four corpus classes equal live G07 v3 by ==, the UNPOPULATED filesystem standing is preserved and even refuses the G22 shortcut, the DR-103 leftovers are explicitly left on CMLJ v4, and the nine obligations bucket cleanly with no misbucket. I must also record that this same defect is present in frozen v1, which I accepted at 0/0: my v1 verdict checked that liveGateOwners carried the single DR-G07 entry and never compared its value against the owner cell I had already parsed. That is a shape-instead-of-content check of the kind I have charged others for, and it is recorded under reviewerSelfCorrection. 18 attacks run, 17 refuted, one landing.
